name: MKI Continue Watching Cleanup
overview: A Remove button on Continue Watching cards, and an optional cleanup of items nobody has touched for a while.
description: Adds a Remove button to the Continue Watching cards of the Jellyfin web client, so people can take things off their own row, with Undo. Optionally clears, once a day, the videos each user has not played for a set number of days (30 by default, 7 at least). Removing only forgets the spot to resume from: files, library entries, watched marks, play counts, favourites and ratings are never touched, and every removal or cleanup run can be undone for 30 days. Everything starts turned off; the plugin changes nothing until an administrator turns a part on.

versions.changelog: First release. A Remove button on Continue Watching cards in the web client (on hover next to Mark played and Favorite, always visible on touch screens), with Undo. Optional daily auto cleanup of videos a user has not played for a set number of days, with a preview of what it would clear, Clean up now, and Undo for every run. Only the resume position is cleared; nothing is deleted or marked as watched. Everything starts turned off.

name: MKI Login Showcase
overview: An animated showcase of your library's artwork behind the Jellyfin sign-in page, in four neon styles.
description: Turns the Jellyfin sign-in page into a showcase of your own library: a drifting poster wall, a slowly zooming backdrop spotlight, a neon horizon with posters gliding along it, or a flip mosaic, with the sign-in form as a neon glass card. You choose which libraries it may show and the highest age rating; titles without a rating, title names and library counts stay hidden unless you turn them on. People who are not signed in only ever get the pictures, never item ids or library names. It respects reduced motion and has calm and still modes for TVs. Everything starts turned off; the sign-in page stays as Jellyfin ships it until an administrator turns the showcase on and picks libraries.

versions.changelog: First release. An animated showcase of library artwork behind the sign-in page in four styles (Poster Wall, Backdrop Spotlight, Neon Horizon, Flip Mosaic) and four neon colour pairs, with the sign-in form as a glass card. You pick the libraries and the highest age rating; unrated titles, title names and library counts stay hidden unless you turn them on. Calm and still motion modes, and reduced motion is respected. Everything starts turned off.

name: MKI Media Hero
overview: A cinematic hero banner on the Jellyfin home screen.
description: Adds a full-width hero carousel to the Jellyfin home screen. The list is prepared on the server from recently added, top rated and (optionally) Seerr trending titles, filtered per library with title, genre, tag and rating whitelists and blacklists. Layout, transitions, text and buttons are configurable.

versions.changelog: New settings page in the shared MKI design, with tabs for Sources, Filters, Look, Details & buttons and Behavior. A live preview draws your own list with the banner's own code at the size of your window and follows every slider while you drag; a small copy stays in the corner while you scroll. The header shows how many titles your list has, how old it is, and how many sources and library places are in use. Text placement is set by dragging the text block, layouts are picked from drawings, and Find a setting jumps to any option. The Seerr address and key can be taken over from MKI Seerr Bridge in one click. Settings save as soon as you change them, with undo, and the list is rebuilt once after each change; turning the banner off asks first. Works on phones and in light and dark themes.

Security update. Every user now gets their own banner that follows their library access, parental controls and blocked tags, instead of one list for everyone, and banners are never shared between accounts in the browser cache. Calls to Seerr no longer follow redirects or keep cookies, and library names on the settings page are escaped.
The API key on the settings page is hidden by default; the eye button shows it.

Cleans up an older copy of this plugin left behind by an update or rename: the old copy is marked for removal and stays inactive, so it can no longer break requests. Restart Jellyfin once to finish the cleanup. Settings are kept.
English only: settings page, labels and log messages are now in English. Redesigned, cleaner settings page with tabs and status indicators. Settings are kept.
Renamed to MKI Media Hero so all MKI plugins sit together in the plugin list. Settings are kept.
Jellyseerr is now Seerr: renamed the trending sources and all labels. Settings are kept.
Per-library targets, sources as upper limits, paged Jellyseerr trending lookup, browser caching and a background pre-warmer.

name: MKI Merge Versions
overview: Two resolutions, one entry. You choose which version leads.
description: Merges movies that exist in several resolutions into a single library entry, matched by TMDb ID (IMDb as fallback), never by title. The highest resolution or the version closest to 1080p becomes the primary version, as you choose. Runs as a scheduled task and automatically once the library has been quiet for five minutes. Includes a dry-run mode.

versions.changelog: New setting: choose the primary version of a merged movie, either 1080p or the highest resolution. The highest resolution stays the default. With "Apply to existing merges" on, the next run switches existing merges to your choice, so a switch to 1080p makes merged movies open and play in their 1080p version. A movie without a 1080p file uses the version closest to it (720p before 4K, 4K before a DVD copy). Favourites, ratings and likes now move with the primary version, so nothing seems lost after a switch. Changing the choice while live asks first.

New settings page in the shared MKI design. The header shows the merge task, the last result, the next run and the primary-version fix at a glance, with Run now and Stop. A timeline shows past and coming runs, and the latest MKI Merge log lines can be shown on demand. Settings save as soon as you change them, with undo; switching from dry run to live asks first. Works on phones and in light and dark themes.

Security update. Versions are only linked when exactly the same users can see them and they share a production year, so merging can no longer reveal a file from a library someone has no access to. Existing links that break this are split again, stale links are released, groups of more than eight versions are skipped, and two runs can no longer overlap.

Cleans up an older copy of this plugin left behind by an update or rename: the old copy is marked for removal and stays inactive, so it can no longer break requests. Restart Jellyfin once to finish the cleanup. Settings are kept.
English only: settings page, labels and log messages are now in English. Redesigned, cleaner settings page with tabs and status indicators. Settings are kept.
First release: links versions via the database, groups by TMDb/IMDb, highest resolution becomes primary, own settings page.

name: MKI Password Policy
overview: Password rules and forced password changes for Jellyfin users.
description: Enforces password rules (length, character types, no username, common passwords) on the server for every client, with ready-made profiles. Lets an administrator require a new password from all users or from single users, right away or with a notice period: they cannot sign in on any device until they have set one. Accounts without a password are locked until they get a temporary password. Web-based apps show a popup users must answer; TVs get Jellyfin's message window and a change page that opens in any browser.

versions.changelog: Leaves guest accounts of MKI Guest Pass alone: they have no password by design, so they are never locked for having none, never asked for a new password, cannot get a temporary password and are left out of the user list and of requests for everyone. Nothing else changes.

New settings page in the shared MKI design, with tabs for Users, Require a new password, Profiles and More settings. The header shows who the rules apply to, the state of everyone's password, open requests and the time left to set a new one. The Users tab lists everyone with search and filters, and flags accounts without a password with a Temporary password button. Before any change that could lock someone out, the page names the accounts and asks; your own account can never be locked from here. A request for everyone shows who gets one and who was already asked, with the notice period chosen in the same dialog. A temporary password is shown once, in a dialog that stays open until you confirm you copied it. Profiles can be compared side by side and tried with a test password, checked in the browser only. Settings save as soon as you change them, with undo. Works on phones and in light and dark themes.

Security update. A blocked user's token is now refused however it is sent (any authorization header, the older header names or the query string), and a request carrying tokens of several users is refused. When a deadline passes, the user's tokens are revoked within a minute, a sign-in that gets through on any path is undone at once, and setting a new password signs out every other device.

Accounts without a password that have a profile or a request are now locked right away on every sign-in path (apps, TVs, Quick Connect, existing sessions), with no notice period, and nobody can claim them by name: new Temporary password button shows a random password once and the user replaces it at the next sign-in. Passwords an administrator sets (Jellyfin's Password tab or new users) and reset PINs now count as temporary for users with a profile. A second request can only bring a deadline forward. Bulk requests never include the admin who sends them. Web-based apps show a popup that must be answered during a notice period; TVs get Jellyfin's message window instead of a fading toast. Settings page: every change applies immediately, no Save button, with a question before anything locks accounts.

New notice period when requiring a new password (right away, or 1, 3, 7 or 14 days): users keep access until the deadline and every app they use, TVs included, shows a message with the deadline and the change link, at most once a day per device. The list shows the deadline and which devices were reminded. New Copy message for users button with a ready text to send.

Disabled users can get profiles and password requests, also from the buttons for many users; they apply once the account is enabled again. With exempt administrators on, administrators are greyed out in the list. Each user's Password tab in the dashboard now shows their profile, password status and any request, with a shortcut to them in the plugin settings. Live hints on that tab now use the rules of the user being edited.

The change dialog now stays above everything, including the Jellyfin loading spinner, and lists the password rules for your account. A profile picked for a user in the list is saved immediately, so requiring a new password right after picking it no longer drops the choice.
All text is now in English.
First release.

name: MKI Screen Fit
overview: Full HD screens play the Full HD version, and transcodes are made only as large as the screen.
description: When a movie has a 4K and a Full HD version (for example merged by MKI Merge Versions) and someone starts it on a screen that cannot show more than Full HD, the Full HD file plays instead, also when the movie plays directly: no transcode of a 4K file for a laptop. Only when both versions are the same cut, the Full HD one has the chosen audio and subtitle language and the player can take it with no more work, and never when someone picked a version by hand. A 4K TV resumes in 4K afterwards. Optionally, a video Jellyfin transcodes anyway (for example for a codec or HDR the device cannot play, burned-in subtitles or a bitrate limit) is transcoded only as large as the screen: a movie that only exists in 4K becomes 1920×1080 instead of 4K on a Full HD laptop, a quarter of the pixels to encode. Browsers and the Jellyfin apps built on the web client measure their screen; for TV apps you choose per device. Bitrate limits and transcode throttling stay exactly as Jellyfin decides. Everything starts turned off.

versions.changelog: Clearer wording on the settings page: the transcode switch is now called "Transcode only as large as the screen" and explains with an example what it does, and the Full HD switch says that it works for direct play too. Nothing else changes.

First release. Plays the Full HD version of a movie with several versions on screens up to 1200 pixels on the shorter side, and can keep re-encoded transcodes no larger than the screen. Browsers and the Jellyfin apps built on the web client report their screen; TV apps can be set per device on the settings page, which also lists recent decisions. Everything starts turned off.

name: MKI Seerr Bridge
overview: Seerr inside Jellyfin: button, embedded view, search and sign-in.
description: Brings Seerr into the Jellyfin web client: a button in the header and side menu, Seerr embedded in Jellyfin instead of a redirect, Seerr suggestions under Jellyfin search results with one-click requests attributed to the right user, optional single sign-on via Quick Connect, and a compatibility bridge for clients that still send legacy X-Emby authorization headers.

versions.changelog: New settings page in the shared MKI design, with tabs for Connection, Menu & search and Sign-in. A diagram shows both roads to Seerr and whether each one answers, a connection test runs by itself after an address change, and the page warns about address problems such as mixed http and https. A sketch shows where the Requests button lands, and Try a search previews the suggestions. Settings save as soon as you change them, with undo; changes that affect requests or sign-in ask first. Works on phones and in light and dark themes.

Security update. Requests from the search results are made in the user's own Seerr account, matched by Jellyfin user ID, and are refused for accounts not linked to Seerr yet instead of running as the administrator; each user can send up to 30 per hour. Single sign-on can no longer be triggered by other websites, and the Seerr session cookie is set HttpOnly (and Secure over https). The settings endpoint needs a signed-in user, the plugin repository answers only inside the local network, the legacy header bridge only passes a single well-formed token, and calls to Seerr no longer follow redirects or keep cookies.
The API key on the settings page is hidden by default; the eye button shows it.

Cleans up an older copy of this plugin left behind by an update or rename: the old copy is marked for removal and stays inactive, so it can no longer break requests. Restart Jellyfin once to finish the cleanup. Settings are kept. Single sign-on now steps aside on any error instead of blocking sign-in.
English only: settings page, labels and log messages are now in English. Redesigned, cleaner settings page with tabs and status indicators. Settings are kept.
Renamed to MKI Seerr Bridge so all MKI plugins sit together in the plugin list. Settings are kept.
Renamed to Seerr Bridge: Jellyseerr is now Seerr. All labels, descriptions and the menu route (#/seerr) follow the new name. Settings are kept.
Header and side-menu button, embedded view, search suggestions with requests, single sign-on via Quick Connect, legacy auth header bridge.
